name: Sparse & Dynamic Top-k Attention
core_idea: Reduce decoding cost by attending to only a subset of KV tokens selected per query, rather than evicting permanently. NSA is natively trainable hierarchical sparse attention (compressed block + fine-grained selected block + sliding window) co-designed with hardware-aligned kernels so sparsity yields real wall-clock speedup. RocketKV's second stage (HSA) does dynamic two-dimensional top-k selection (sequence + head) using page-wise K_max/K_min statistics, and Quest/SparQ are single-dimension precursors. The route is distinct from eviction because selection is per-query and dynamic, and from architecture because it keeps standard attention over a filtered set.
